feedback.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}x+\frac{1}{3}y=-1 \\ x+\frac{3}{7}y=\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.
feedback.worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $3$ and the second equation by $7,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}x+\frac{1}{3}y=-1 & |\times 3 \\ x+\frac{3}{7}y=\frac{1}{7} & |\times 7\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}4x+y=-3 \\ 7x+3y=1\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Notice that the first equation can easily be solved for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+y & =-3 \\ y & =-3-4x\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute $y=-3-4x$ into the second equation and then solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}7x+3y & =1 \\ 7x+3(-3-4x) & =1 \\ 7x-9-12x & =1 \\ -5x & =10 \\ x & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $y,$ we substitute $x=-2$ into the equation $y=-3-4x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-3-4x \\  & =-3-4(-2) \\  & =-3+8 \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=-2$ and $y=5.$
